title: Video understanding: frames, transcription and summarising

videos.script: A video looks like one thing. To a program, it is two. A stream of pictures, and a stream of sound. {{title}} No model reads every picture. Thirty-two seconds of Marginalia's returns video is eight hundred and fifteen frames. {{frames}} So you choose which pictures to look at. Every few seconds, or wherever the picture changes. {{sample}} Then you listen to the soundtrack, and you put the two side by side, on one timeline. {{timeline}} The video in this lesson hides something on purpose. A card that is on screen for less than half a second, and that nobody says out loud. {{card}} Sampling at a fixed rate misses it. Listening misses it too. Only looking where the picture changes finds it. {{find}} By the end you will know how to turn a video into something a model can read. You will also know what that version leaves out. {{end}}
